judged_text: The generic 'access token + expiry' sync payload doesn't match the provider-specific parsers of the fetch-based consumers either (Lark's {code, msg, data} envelope; Zoom/O365/MS-Teams schemas requiring refresh_token/expires_in), so even the consistent call sites fail to parse it.

adjudication.rationale: The new sync mode in `refreshOAuthTokens` explicitly returns a response from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` whose body is expected to be a generic "access token + expiry" payload (see comment in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). However, several consumers still pass the returned response through provider-specific response handlers/parsers (e.g., Lark calls `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, ...)` in `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, which implies a Lark-specific envelope), and others still rely on provider-shaped token responses unless adapted. Only some integrations were updated to use `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (Zoom/O365/Google/Salesforce), so the generic sync payload can fail to parse/handle correctly for integrations that still expect provider-specific structures.
